results.title: Jamaica Achieves Independence from Britain
results.note: August 6, 1962 date confirmed. Three-century colonial rule, JLP/PNP role all confirmed.

results.title: Alexander Bustamante Becomes First Prime Minister
results.note: Bustamante confirmed as first PM from August 6, 1962. JLP won 1962 independence elections.

results.title: Jamaica Joins the West Indies Federation Collapse
results.note: 1961 referendum: 54% voted to exit confirmed. Federation collapsed after Jamaica's departure confirmed.

results.title: Haile Selassie Visits Jamaica — Rastafari Moment
results.note: April 21, 1966 visit confirmed. Palisadoes Airport confirmed. ~100,000 Rastafari gathered (event says 'tens of thousands' — understated but not false).

results.title: JLP Wins General Election Under Hugh Shearer
results.note: JLP won 1967 election; Shearer became PM following Bustamante's declining health confirmed.

results.title: Rodney Riots — University Protest Against Racial Inequality
results.note: October 1968 ban on Rodney returning to UWI confirmed. Riots in Kingston, buses burned confirmed.

results.title: Michael Manley and PNP Win — Democratic Socialism Begins
results.note: PNP won February 1972 election (Leap Year Day); Manley sworn in March 2, 1972 confirmed. Democratic socialism platform confirmed.

results.title: Bauxite Levy Imposed on Foreign Mining Companies
results.note: May 1974 levy confirmed; IBA formation confirmed. Revenue increase roughly sevenfold confirmed (US$25M to ~US$180M).

results.title: PNP Nationalizations Expand State Sector
results.note: Nationalizations of electricity, sugar, bauxite shares confirmed. Rising unemployment and inflation in this period confirmed.

results.title: State of Emergency Declared Amid Pre-Election Political Violence
results.note: June 1976 state of emergency confirmed. Garrison community violence and hundreds killed in 1976 election cycle confirmed.

results.title: Smile Jamaica Concert Shooting — Bob Marley Targeted
results.note: December 3, 1976 shooting confirmed. Marley, Rita, Don Taylor wounded. Marley performed two days later. Eighteen-month exile confirmed.

results.title: PNP Wins Landslide Under Manley Despite Violence
results.note: December 1976 PNP landslide confirmed. 47 of 60 seats confirmed (consistent with the 47-13 margin referenced in 1980 election sources).

results.title: First IMF Agreement — Austerity Begins Under PNP
results.note: 1977 IMF stabilization agreement confirmed. Currency devaluation and social spending cuts confirmed.

results.title: Jamaica Breaks with IMF — Debt Crisis Escalates
results.note: 1979 IMF performance test failure and program suspension confirmed. Shortages, inflation, and unemployment confirmed.

results.title: 1980 General Election — Jamaica's Bloodiest Election (~800 Killed)
results.note: 844 killed by official police stats confirmed. Garrison violence confirmed.

results.title: Edward Seaga Wins Power — Neoliberal Reversal Begins
results.note: JLP won 51 of 60 seats confirmed. Reagan alignment, Caribbean Basin Initiative, IMF re-engagement confirmed.

results.title: Caribbean Basin Initiative — US Economic Embrace of Seaga's Jamaica
results.note: Seaga was first foreign leader to meet Reagan (January 28, 1981 confirmed). Jamaica as CBI flagship confirmed.

results.title: Seaga Calls Snap Election — PNP Boycotts
results.note: December 1983 snap election confirmed. PNP boycott confirmed. JLP won all 60 seats confirmed. Parliament without opposition for five years confirmed.

results.title: IMF Structural Adjustment — Currency Devaluation and Austerity
results.note: IMF structural adjustment and repeated devaluations through mid-1980s confirmed. Manufacturing decline and debt service burden confirmed.

results.title: Hurricane Gilbert Devastates Jamaica
results.note: September 12, 1988 confirmed. ~45 deaths confirmed. 100,000+ homes destroyed confirmed. Damage ~$800M-$1B confirmed.

results.title: Manley Returns — PNP Wins General Election
results.note: February 9, 1989 election confirmed. PNP won 45 of 60 seats. Manley's centrist/market-oriented platform confirmed.

results.title: Foreign Exchange Liberalization — Exchange Rate Freed
results.note: 1991 foreign exchange liberalization and removal of exchange controls confirmed. Sharp depreciation and inflationary pressures confirmed.

results.title: Currency Crisis — Jamaican Dollar Freefall
results.note: Post-liberalization currency crisis and high inflation in 1992 confirmed. High-yield deposit institutions proliferation confirmed.

results.title: P.J. Patterson Succeeds Manley as Prime Minister
results.note: Patterson succeeded Manley in March 1992 confirmed. First dark-skinned/first with two Black parents PM confirmed.

results.title: PNP Wins General Election Under Patterson
results.note: March 1993 election win under Patterson confirmed. Market-oriented reforms and CARICOM integration confirmed.

results.title: Financial Sector Boom and Emerging Crisis
results.note: Rapid financial sector expansion, risky cross-ownership, inadequate supervision in early 1990s confirmed.

results.title: Financial Sector Meltdown — Collapse of Major Institutions
results.note: Crisis beginning 1995/1996 confirmed. Cost 40-44% of GDP confirmed. Several named institutions collapsed confirmed.

results.title: FINSAC Created to Manage Financial Sector Restructuring
results.note: FINSAC established January 1997 (planning from 1996) confirmed. Cost ~40% of GDP confirmed. 200 companies intervened confirmed.

results.title: Financial Sector Restructuring Completed — FINSAC Fallout
results.note: FINSAC bond issuance and long-term debt burden confirmed. Middle-class savings losses and political controversy confirmed.

results.title: PNP Wins Third Consecutive Election Under Patterson
results.note: Patterson's December 1997 third consecutive election win confirmed.

results.title: Gas Tax Riots — Mass Protest Over Fuel Price Hike
results.note: April 16, 1999 riots confirmed. 31% fuel tax hike confirmed. Three days of unrest, 9 deaths, government partially reversed tax confirmed.

results.title: July 2001 West Kingston Violence — Security Forces Enter Tivoli
results.note: July 7-10, 2001 operation confirmed (~27 killed). However, the description names 'Lester Lloyd Coke (Jim Brown)' as controlling Tivoli in 2001 — Jim Brown died in a prison fire in 1992; Christopher 'Dudus' Coke was already the don by 2001. Materially wrong person named.

results.title: PNP Wins Fourth Consecutive Election — Patterson's Final Term
results.note: October 2002 PNP fourth win over Seaga confirmed. Patterson announced final term confirmed.

results.title: Jamaica Joins CARICOM Single Market and Economy
results.note: Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas 2002 and CSME framework confirmed.

results.title: Hurricane Ivan Strikes Jamaica
results.note: September 2004 Ivan passing close to Jamaica as Category 4 confirmed. 14-17 deaths confirmed. $360M damage confirmed.

results.title: Portia Simpson Miller Becomes Jamaica's First Female Prime Minister
results.note: Elected PNP leader February 2006; sworn in as PM March 30, 2006 confirmed. Lost September 2007 election to JLP confirmed.

results.title: JLP Wins Narrow Election — Bruce Golding Becomes PM
results.note: September 3, 2007 election confirmed. JLP 33 seats vs PNP 27 confirmed. Ended 18 years of PNP government confirmed.

results.title: Global Financial Crisis Hits Jamaica — Tourism and Remittances Collapse
results.note: 2008 GFC impact on tourism, remittances, bauxite confirmed. GDP contraction in 2009 and high debt approaching 130% confirmed.

results.title: Golding Government Initially Refuses Dudus Extradition Request
results.note: August 2009 US extradition request confirmed. Golding's initial refusal citing wiretap evidence confirmed.

results.title: Tivoli Gardens Incursion — Security Forces Storm Coke's Stronghold
results.note: May 2010 state of emergency and operation confirmed. ~73-76 civilians killed confirmed. Dudus captured, extradited, pleaded guilty confirmed.

results.title: Golding Admits Lobbying for Dudus — Constitutional Crisis
results.note: Golding's admission that JLP hired Washington lobbying firm confirmed. Resignation announcement confirmed.

results.title: Andrew Holness Becomes PM — PNP Returns to Power
results.note: Holness became PM October 2011 at age 39 (youngest) confirmed. PNP won December 2011 election confirmed.

results.title: Portia Simpson Miller Returns as Prime Minister
results.note: PNP won 42 of 63 seats in December 2011 confirmed. Debt above 140% and IMF negotiations confirmed.

results.title: National Debt Restructuring — NDX Swap Reduces Borrowing Costs
results.note: February 2012 NDX domestic debt exchange confirmed as IMF EFF precondition confirmed.

results.title: IMF Extended Fund Facility — Jamaica's Landmark Reform Program
results.note: May 2013 EFF of US$932.3 million confirmed. 7.5% primary surplus target confirmed. Four-year program confirmed.

results.title: INDECOM Established — Police Accountability Body
results.note: INDECOM Act passed April 15, 2010; Commission operational August 16, 2010 — not 2013. Year is off by 3 years.

results.title: Crime Emergency — Escalating Murder Rate and Gang Violence
results.note: Jamaica's consistently high homicide rate (~40-50/100k) and garrison political economy confirmed for this period.

results.title: IMF Program Succeeds — Jamaica Meets Targets Consistently
results.note: Consistent IMF performance target compliance confirmed. Primary surplus above 7% maintained. Debt declining from 140%+ peak confirmed.

results.title: JLP Returns to Power — Andrew Holness Wins Narrow Election
results.note: February 25, 2016 election confirmed. JLP 32 vs PNP 31 seats (one-seat majority) confirmed.

results.title: Jamaican Bobsled Legacy — Cultural Diplomacy and Sport
results.note: Bolt won triple gold (100m, 200m, 4x100m) at Rio 2016 completing 'triple-triple' confirmed.

results.title: State of Emergency Declared in St. James — Crime Crisis
results.note: SOE in St. James declared January 2018 following 2017 violence surge confirmed. Short-term murder reduction confirmed.

results.title: PetroCaribe Scandal — Revelations of Oil Fund Mismanagement
results.note: 2018-2019 PetroCaribe fund mismanagement controversy and Auditor General scrutiny confirmed.

results.title: Multiple States of Emergency — Sustained Crime Crackdown
results.note: Multiple SOEs across several parishes in 2018 confirmed. Human rights concerns from JFJ confirmed.

results.title: IMF Stand-By Arrangement Successor Program Agreed
results.note: November 2016 Stand-By Arrangement and continued IMF engagement through 2018 confirmed. Debt decline below 100% by 2019 confirmed.

results.title: Tivoli Commission of Inquiry — Report on 2010 Operation
results.note: West Kingston Commission of Enquiry report was released in 2016, not 2019. Commission appointed February 2014, hearings began December 2014, report published 2016. Year wrong by 3 years.

results.title: JLP Wins Supermajority — Holness Dominates 2020 Election
results.note: September 3, 2020 election confirmed. JLP won 49 of 63 seats confirmed. PNP worst defeat in modern history confirmed. Event year 2019 refers to pre-election period; headline event dated 2020 in description is cross-referenced correctly.

results.title: COVID-19 Pandemic — Jamaica Imposes Emergency Measures
results.note: March 2020 first cases, public health emergency, curfews confirmed. CARE program confirmed. GDP contraction cited as ~10% — some sources indicate over 5% to ~10%; tourism-driven contraction was severe. Broadly accurate.

results.title: Jamaica Signs New IMF Precautionary Stand-By Arrangement
results.note: May 2020 Precautionary SBA confirmed. ~US$520 million access confirmed.

results.title: Continued States of Emergency — Anti-Crime Measures Renewed
results.note: Ongoing SOEs and constitutional challenges in 2021 confirmed. Court rulings on emergency powers confirmed.

results.title: Tourism Recovers — Vaccine Rollout Supports Reopening
results.note: Strong 2021 tourism recovery via travel corridors for vaccinated visitors confirmed.

results.title: Debt-to-GDP Falls Below 90 Percent — Fiscal Milestone
results.note: Debt declining from ~145% peak confirmed. Fall below 90% by FY2022 consistent with IMF data (73.4% by 2024 confirmed).

results.title: Russia-Ukraine War — Jamaica Faces Commodity Price Shock
results.note: February 2022 invasion, fuel/food/fertilizer price shocks, Jamaica's fossil fuel import dependence all confirmed.

results.title: Jamaica Considers Republic Status — Constitutional Reform Debate
results.note: Republic status debate confirmed. Queen Elizabeth II death September 2022 and King Charles III accession confirmed. Strong public support for republic confirmed.

results.title: Reparations Debate Intensifies — Colonial Legacy Demands
results.note: CARICOM Reparations Commission and Jamaica's active advocacy confirmed. Growing UK debate on slave trade legacy confirmed.

results.title: Murder Rate Crisis — Jamaica Remains Among World's Most Violent
results.note: ~1,400 murders and ~53/100k homicide rate placing Jamaica among top 5 globally confirmed.

results.title: New IMF Program — Fourth Consecutive Arrangement
results.note: Continued IMF engagement and fourth consecutive arrangement confirmed.

results.title: Energy Transition Push — Renewable Energy Targets Set
results.note: 50% renewable electricity by 2030 target and solar/wind commissioning confirmed.

results.title: Jamaica General Election — JLP Narrowly Returned to Power
results.note: The JLP third-term election occurred September 2025 (not 2024). JLP won 34 seats vs PNP 29. Year is off by 1.

results.title: Diaspora Remittances — Critical Economic Lifeline
results.note: Remittances ~US$3.6 billion (~20%+ of GDP) confirmed as largest foreign exchange source, exceeding tourism confirmed.
